text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: P1 detected — Elevated 5xx/timeouts from transit gateway in us-west1.  Ops: 502/504 spike and long tail latencies starting ~11:01Z. Auto-paged on-call.

Devon (oncall): looking now. confirming increased 5xx and gateway-level timeouts. tagging logs + grafana.

Ron P: grabbing logs. seeing a lot of upstream 502/504 to our backend pool (model-router-usw1). snippet:

```
[2026-03-14T11:02:03Z] route=transit-gw-usw1 upstream=10.12.5.22 upstream_response_status=502 upstream_latency=120ms req_id=abc123
[2026-03-14T11:02:04Z] route=transit-gw-usw1 upstream=10.12.5.33 upstream_response_status=504 upstream_latency=5s req_id=abc124
[2026-03-14T11:02:05Z] route=transit-gw-usw1 backend_error=true error_kind=connection-reset
```

Jess L: dashboards show 5xx rate from us-west1 jumped from ~0.5% to ~18% at 11:01Z. p95 latency on the gateway jumped to 3.2s. throughput steady.

Maria S: early customer impact check — ~12 hosted API keys seeing elevated errors (mostly generation endpoints). Notifying support to patch tickets.

Devon (oncall): hypothesis — either backend model-router instances are overloaded or the transit-gateway sync agent is stalling connections causing long timeouts. We should divert traffic and scale backend pools.

SRE Pager: recommended mitigations: 1) shift routing for non-residency customers to eu-west1 fallback 2) scale model-router-usw1 pool 3) add temporary connection retry/backoff config.

Alex K: agree. doing a staged traffic shift. first to 40% to eu-west1 then monitor. Command: 
```
redwoodctl route shift --from-region=us-west1 --to-region=eu-west1 --percent=40 --scope=non-residency --note="mitigate transit gateway 5xx spike"
```

Ron P: scaling model-router in us-west1 now (k8s):
```
kubectl -n infra scale deploy model-router-usw1 --replicas=10
kubectl -n infra rollout status deploy/model-router-usw1
```

Devon (oncall): also bumping gateway connection_pool limits to reduce resets. Applying a short-lived config: `gateway.conn_pool.max=500` across transit-gw-usw1.

Jess L: after the 40% shift we see overall 5xx drop from 18% -> 9% in 3m. p95 latency trending down. good signal.

Maria S: drafting statuspage: "We are experiencing elevated errors in us-west1. A partial failover to eu-west1 is in progress for affected customers. No data loss. Monitoring closely." Sharing to #status-desk in 10m unless more impact.

Ron P: logs still show some backend connection resets; investigating upstream health checks. Looks like a subset of backend instances had networking flaps with our autoscaler. Collecting `tcpdump` and healthcheck traces.

Devon (oncall): ok keep shift at 40% for now. Alex, can you continue on traffic ops? I'll dig into autoscaler + CNI flaps.

Alex K: confirming. increasing shift to 75% to accelerate mitigation for most traffic (non-residency). Running: 
```
redwoodctl route shift --from-region=us-west1 --to-region=eu-west1 --percent=75 --now
```

IncidentBot: Action logged: route shift to eu-west1 (75%) by Alex K.

Jess L: 5xx now at ~3.1% across platform, us-west1 at 7%. p95 down to 1.1s. good.

SRE Pager: recommend keeping scaling and monitoring for 30m then plan rollback when stable. Also propose a targeted restart of the problematic model-router instances after draining connections.

Ron P: completing drains now for 3 unhealthy pods and redeploying the autoscaler config with a fix for probe thresholds. commands: 
```
kubectl -n infra cordon pod/model-router-7f8d
kubectl -n infra drain pod/model-router-7f8d --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl -n infra delete pod/model-router-7f8d
```

Devon (oncall): I started the deeper triage: CNI plugin had a regression from yesterday's platform update that caused sporadic conntrack exhaustion under certain routing table churn. Opening a follow-up ticket to rollback that change in a maintenance window.

Maria S: support notified affected customers and applied temporary workarounds for enterprise customers requiring no cross-region routing. One customer asked for SLA credit — flagging to CS.

Alex K: as traffic stabilizes I'm going to slowly move shift back once cluster health is green. Plan: 75% -> 50% (15m) -> 25% (20m) -> 0 with monitoring gates.

Jess L: gate checks good at 15m and 30m. At 30m us-west1 5xx at 0.8% and overall p95 0.45s.

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved — error rates returned to baseline, routing restored. Root cause: CNI/conntrack exhaustion on a subset of us-west1 nodes after yesterday's platform update. Impact: partial regional degradation for 25-40% of traffic for ~28 minutes.

Devon (oncall): handoff to Alex K for postmortem and next steps (rollback plan + improved healthchecks). I'll file the incident ticket with logs and tcpdumps.

Alex K: will own postmortem. action items: 1) revert or patch CNI change 2) increase conntrack defaults in baseline AMI 3) add automated probe to detect conntrack exhaustion earlier 4) improve routing fallback runbook to avoid risk for data-residency customers.

Maria S: I'll coordinate customer comms and SLA follow-ups.

SRE Pager: closing pager. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Alex K: noted. great cross-team response — thanks team.
